Definition: of uncertain affinity; the tongue; by implication, a language (specially, one naturally unacquired):--tongue.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, glōssa is the word for tongue. In Mark 7:33, the text says "and touched his tongue." In Luke 1:64, the text says "and his tongue [loosed."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, glōssa is a reminder that truth is not whatever we feel; it is what God has said, and it stands. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Pentecost; The Birth of John the Baptist; Jesus Heals a Deaf and Mute Man in the Decapolis
